A stack-based buffer overflow vulnerability exists in a FirePass web browser plug-in. This plug-in is installed on a Mozilla-based web browser (such as Firefox) when a user logs on to the FirePass controller. In some configurations, this plug-in may be installed at the FirePass logon page prior to authentication. It is possible for an attacker to create a web page that causes a buffer overflow in the affected plug-in, resulting in arbitrary code execution on the client machine.

In order for this exploit to be successful, the attacker must persuade you to view the malicious web page. If you view the malicious web page in a browser that has affected FirePass plug-in installed, this could result in malicious code execution on the client side, disclosure of sensitive information, or other exploits.

F5 Product Development tracked this issue as CR67293 and CR68939, and it is fixed in FirePass 5.5.2 and 6.0.1. For information about upgrading, refer to the FirePass Release Notes.

Additionally, a hotfix has been issued for version 6.0 of FirePass software. For FirePass 6.0, this issue was fixed in cumulative hotfix HF-600-4. You may download this hotfix or later versions of the cumulative hotfix from the F5 Downloads site. For information about the F5 hotfix policy, refer to K4918: Overview of F5 Networks critical issue hotfix policy.
